defaults._coverage_scope: measured on the ENGINE (qa_ledger.py) through the smoke run() choke point (~370 subprocess calls); since 1.82.0 (D-03) on the auxiliary scripts (templates/scripts, mirador render) through runpy() -- each --source derived from the script own dirname because coverage.py --source is last-wins, not additive; and since 1.90.0 through two more: pyin(), which spools a heredoc driver to a file so coverage run can take a program stdin cannot give it (this is what finally measured uscha_top.py, driven in-process by 24 acceptance criteria and reported at 0% until then), and coverage.py's documented multiprocess hook (COVERAGE_PROCESS_START plus an rc carrying the source roots as a list), which reaches the engine children that test blocks spawn from INSIDE their own python -- the shape most blocks written since ~T117 use, and the reason cmd_fastpath_eval read 1/132 covered lines while nine criteria were measured against it. Note what that hook really is: coverage.py 7.x ships a1_coverage.pth in site-packages and a .pth runs BEFORE sitecustomize, so the variable alone instruments EVERY python descendant; the sitecustomize the suite writes is only the portable fallback for a build without that .pth, and it cannot opt a process out. The blast radius is bounded at the one boundary where it matters: qa_ledger.py _judged_env() drops the coverage start-up variables from the environment of a program the withheld oracle is judging (T127 pins it) -- without that, ~14,000 fixture children were instrumented to record nothing (combine: 600 files kept, 13702 skipped) and Windows eventually refused to create processes, which surfaced as seven bench archetypes flipping to FAIL and a py3.8 interpreter exiting 0xC0000142. Regenerate: USCHA_COVERAGE=1 bash uscha-kit/tests/smoke-engine.sh, then coverage combine && coverage xml --ignore-errors --omit='*/.coverage-data/*' -o reports/coverage.xml. The --omit drops the harness's own sitecustomize shim, which is not kit code. --ignore-errors is kept as a cheap guard but is no longer required: the reason it existed (a golden-coverage capture leaking a sitecustomize.py from an already-deleted temp dir into the shared data file) is gone since the 1.90.0 AC-GM-08 fix pinned that capture to its own data file -- measured, coverage xml now exits 0 without it. Under USCHA_COVERAGE=1 the suite reads the same criteria as the plain suite (1.90.0); the plain suite is still the gate.
